title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
objective: Talk about habits and facts (present simple) and about actions happening now or temporary situations (present continuous).

sections.heading: Present simple — habits, routines, facts
sections.en: Use the present simple for things that are always or usually true. Add -s / -es with he, she, it.
sections.fr: Le présent simple exprime une habitude ou une vérité générale. N'oubliez pas le -s à la 3e personne du singulier.
examples: I work in Lomé.
She takes the bus every morning.
Water boils at 100 °C.
He doesn't drink coffee.
Do you speak English?

sections.heading: Present continuous — now and temporary
sections.en: Use am / is / are + verb-ing for actions in progress now or for temporary situations.
sections.fr: Le présent continu (be + -ing) décrit une action en cours ou une situation temporaire. Le français utilise souvent « en train de ».
examples: I'm reading an article right now.
They are working on a new project this month.
Look! It's raining.
She isn't sleeping — she's studying.

sections.heading: Signal words
sections.en: Some time expressions help you choose.
table: always, usually, often, every day, on Mondays, never
now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!

sections.heading: State verbs
sections.en: Verbs of thinking, feeling and possession (know, like, want, need, believe, understand, own) are normally NOT used in the continuous form.
sections.fr: Les verbes d'état ne se mettent pas à la forme -ing : on dit « I know », jamais « I am knowing ».
examples: I understand the question. (not: I am understanding)
He wants a new laptop.

vocab.example: I usually wake up at six.

vocab.definition: to travel regularly between home and work
the time by which something must be finished
vocab.example: We are working late because of a deadline.

practice.prompt: Every morning, Koffi ___ to the office by taxi-moto.
practice.explanation: "Every morning" = routine → present simple. He/she/it takes -s/-es: go → goes.
Action happening right now → present continuous: is sleeping.
Negative present simple: subject + does not + base verb (like, not likes).

quiz.prompt: I ___ English three times a week.
quiz.explanation: "Three times a week" is a frequency → present simple. With "I" there is no -s.

quiz.prompt: Look! The bus ___.
quiz.explanation: "Look!" shows an action happening now → present continuous.

quiz.prompt: I ___ what you mean.
quiz.explanation: "Understand" is a state verb: no continuous form.

quiz.prompt: My brother ___ (not / work) this week because he is on holiday.
quiz.explanation: "This week" + temporary situation → present continuous negative: is not working.

quiz.prompt: ___ your sister speak French? (do / does)
quiz.explanation: Questions in the present simple with he/she/it use "does" + base verb.

quiz.prompt: "She watch TV every evening" is correct.
quiz.explanation: Third person singular needs -es: She watches TV every evening.

quiz.prompt: We ___ a new app this month. It's a big project.
Make a question.

rememberErrors.why: Don't forget -s with he/she/it in the present simple.
State verbs (know, like, want, need…) are not used with -ing.
After does/doesn't, use the base verb (no -s).

title: Everyday English: your daily routine
objective: Describe your day clearly with common routine verbs and time expressions.

sections.heading: Routine verbs
sections.en: Many routine verbs are phrasal verbs (verb + particle). Learn them as one unit.
sections.fr: Beaucoup de verbes du quotidien sont des « phrasal verbs » : apprenez-les en bloc.
examples: I wake up at 5:30 and get up at 5:45.
I get dressed, have breakfast and leave home at 7.
In the evening I go back home, have a shower and go to bed around 11.

sections.heading: Time expressions
sections.en: Use "in" with parts of the day, "at" with clock times and night, "on" with days.
sections.fr: in the morning / at 7 o'clock / at night / on Monday.
table: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening
at 7 a.m., at noon, at night, at the weekend (UK)
on Monday, on Friday evening, on 12 May

vocab.example: I wake up before my alarm.
I get up at six on weekdays.

vocab.definition: to eat the first meal of the day
vocab.context: Meals — we "have" meals, we don't "take" them

vocab.definition: the busy time when people travel to or from work
vocab.example: Traffic is terrible during rush hour.

vocab.definition: a day when you do not work

vocab.example: I get home at about 7 p.m.

vocab.definition: regular jobs at home, like cleaning
vocab.example: I do the chores on Saturday.

vocab.definition: to sleep for a short time during the day
vocab.example: I sometimes take a nap after lunch.

quiz.prompt: My alarm rings and I ___. Then I get up.
quiz.explanation: "Wake up" = stop sleeping; "get up" = leave the bed.

quiz.prompt: I ___ home at 6 p.m.
I have English classes ___ Tuesday evening.
quiz.explanation: "On" + day (even with a part of the day): on Tuesday evening.

quiz.prompt: The roads are full during ___ hour.
Saturday is my ___. I don't work.
"I do the chores" means I do jobs like cleaning and washing at home.

title: Introducing yourself professionally
objective: Introduce yourself, your studies and your job in 4–5 clear sentences.

sections.heading: A simple structure
sections.en: Name → where you are from / live → what you do → one detail → a goal.
sections.fr: Une structure simple et efficace : nom, origine, activité, un détail, un objectif.
examples: Hi, I'm Ama. I'm from Kara, but I live in Lomé.
I'm a software developer and I work for a small company.
At the moment I'm studying for a master's degree in data science.
In my free time I enjoy football and reading.
I'm learning English because I want to study abroad.

sections.heading: Job vs. work
sections.en: "Job" is a countable noun (a job). "Work" is usually uncountable (I have a lot of work). Say "I work as a developer" or "I'm a developer".
sections.fr: « a job » (dénombrable) / « work » (indénombrable). « I work as a… » = je travaille comme…

vocab.example: I work as a data analyst.
She has a degree in economics.

vocab.definition: to live or work mainly in a place
vocab.example: Our company is based in Lomé.

vocab.definition: when I am not working or studying
vocab.example: In my free time I play football.

options: I am the developer of job.
practice.explanation: Jobs need "a/an": I am a developer. "Work like" means "in the same way as"; use "work as".

quiz.prompt: I work ___ a project manager.
I'm looking for a new ___.
Our studio ___ Lomé.
quiz.explanation: Fixed expression: to be based in + city.

quiz.prompt: "I have 28 years" is the correct way to say your age.
Put the words in order.
quiz.answer: I am learning English to study abroad

title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
objective: Tell a short story: finished actions (past simple) and background actions in progress (past continuous).

sections.heading: Past simple — finished actions
sections.en: Regular verbs add -ed (worked, studied, stopped). Many common verbs are irregular (go → went, see → saw, have → had). Negatives and questions use did + base verb.
sections.fr: Le prétérit exprime une action terminée à un moment précis du passé. Après « did/didn't », le verbe reste à la base verbale.
examples: I visited Accra last year.
She didn't go to work yesterday.
Did you see the match?
We had a meeting on Monday.

sections.heading: Past continuous — the background
sections.en: was / were + verb-ing describes an action in progress at a moment in the past, often interrupted by a short action in the past simple.
sections.fr: Le passé continu (was/were + -ing) correspond souvent à l'imparfait : il décrit le décor, l'action en cours.
examples: I was working when the power went off.
At 8 p.m. yesterday we were watching the news.
While she was driving, her phone rang.

sections.heading: when / while
sections.en: "While" + long action (past continuous). "When" + short action (past simple).

sections.heading: Frequent irregular verbs
sections.en: Learn these first.

vocab.definition: a time when there is no electricity
vocab.example: There was a power cut during the exam.
I started English two years ago.
At first, the job was difficult.

practice.explanation: Background action interrupted by "you called" → past continuous: was watching (I → was).

quiz.prompt: She ___ to Ghana two years ago.
quiz.explanation: "Two years ago" = finished time → past simple.

quiz.prompt: We ___ (not / have) time to finish the report.
quiz.explanation: Negative past simple: did not + base verb (have, not had).

quiz.prompt: While I ___, I saw an accident.
___ you finish your homework yesterday?
quiz.explanation: Past simple questions: Did + subject + base verb.

quiz.prompt: The power ___ (go) off while we were working.
quiz.explanation: Short action interrupting the background → past simple: went.

quiz.prompt: "Did you went to the meeting?" is correct.
quiz.explanation: After "did", use the base verb: Did you go…?

quiz.prompt: At 9 o'clock last night, they ___ dinner.
quiz.explanation: Action in progress at a precise past moment → past continuous; they → were.

quiz.prompt: I ___ (buy) a new phone last week.

rememberErrors.why: "Ago" for a point in the past, after the time expression.

rememberErrors.wrong: When I was cooking, the phone was ringing.
rememberErrors.right: While I was cooking, the phone rang.
rememberErrors.why: The short event is in the past simple.

title: Travel: at the airport and on the road
objective: Understand and use the key words you need at an airport, a hotel and when asking for directions.

sections.heading: At the airport
sections.en: You check in, go through security, wait at the gate and board the plane. Your luggage is uncountable: one bag, two pieces of luggage.
sections.fr: « luggage » et « baggage » sont indénombrables : pas de -s.
examples: Where can I check in for the flight to Paris?
My flight is delayed by two hours.
Boarding starts at gate 12.

sections.heading: Polite requests
sections.en: Use "Could you…?" or "Can I…?" + please.
examples: Could you tell me where the taxi rank is?
Can I have a window seat, please?
Excuse me, how do I get to the city centre?

vocab.definition: to register at an airport or hotel
vocab.example: We checked in two hours before the flight.

vocab.definition: the document you need to get on a plane

vocab.example: How much luggage can I take?

vocab.definition: the place in an airport where you get on the plane
to reserve a room, seat or ticket
vocab.example: I booked a hotel near the station.

vocab.definition: a ticket to go somewhere and come back (US: round-trip)

practice.explanation: Luggage is uncountable: use "pieces of luggage" or "bags".

quiz.prompt: You need your ___ to get on the plane.
quiz.explanation: The boarding pass is the document for boarding.

quiz.prompt: I'd like to ___ a room for two nights.
The flight is ___: it will leave at 10 instead of 8.
quiz.explanation: Delayed = late. Cancelled = it will not happen.

quiz.prompt: ___ tell me where gate 5 is?
quiz.explanation: Polite request: Could you + base verb?

quiz.prompt: "How much luggages do you have?" is correct.
quiz.explanation: No plural: How much luggage do you have?

title: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous
objective: Choose the right future form for plans, decisions, predictions and arrangements.

sections.heading: going to — plans and evidence
sections.en: Use am/is/are going to + verb for intentions decided before now, and for predictions based on what you see.
sections.fr: « be going to » = intention déjà décidée, ou prédiction fondée sur un indice visible.
examples: I'm going to apply for a scholarship next year.
Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.

sections.heading: will — instant decisions, promises, opinions about the future
sections.en: Use will + base verb for decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers, promises and predictions based on opinion.
sections.fr: « will » = décision prise sur le moment, promesse, offre, prédiction d'opinion.
examples: The phone is ringing — I'll answer it.
I'll send you the file tonight, I promise.
I think AI will change many jobs.

sections.heading: Present continuous — fixed arrangements
sections.en: For arrangements with a time and other people (meetings, appointments, travel).
sections.fr: Le présent continu exprime un rendez-vous ou un arrangement déjà organisé.
examples: I'm meeting the client on Thursday at 10.
We're flying to Abidjan tomorrow.

vocab.definition: money given to a student to pay for studies
vocab.example: She got a scholarship to study in Canada.

vocab.definition: to formally ask for a job, a place, etc.
vocab.example: I'm going to apply for a master's programme.

vocab.definition: a fixed time to meet someone
vocab.example: I have an appointment with the dentist.

practice.prompt: "It's cold in here." — "I ___ close the window."
practice.explanation: Instant decision at the moment of speaking → will ('ll).

quiz.prompt: I've decided. I ___ study in Canada next year.
quiz.explanation: Plan decided before speaking → going to.

quiz.prompt: I ___ my manager at 3 p.m. — it's in our calendars.
quiz.explanation: Fixed arrangement with a time → present continuous.

quiz.prompt: Don't worry, I ___ tell anyone.
Be careful! You ___ fall! (going to)
quiz.explanation: Prediction based on visible evidence → going to.

quiz.prompt: "I will to call you tomorrow" is correct.
quiz.explanation: No "to" after will: I will call you.

quiz.prompt: I think robots ___ do many jobs in 2050.
quiz.explanation: Opinion about the future ("I think") → will + base verb.

rememberErrors.why: Modal verbs are followed by the base verb, without "to".
Present simple is not used for personal future plans.

title: Work and careers
objective: Talk about your job, your tasks and your career goals.

sections.heading: Talking about your job
sections.en: Say what you are responsible for and what you deal with.
examples: I'm in charge of the mobile team.
I'm responsible for testing new features.
I deal with clients every day.

sections.heading: Career goals
sections.en: Use "I'd like to…", "My goal is to…", "I'm planning to…".
examples: My goal is to become a data engineer.
I'd like to work for an international company.

vocab.definition: to be responsible for something or someone
vocab.example: She is in charge of the budget.

vocab.definition: money you receive regularly for your job

vocab.example: This job requires good communication skills.
The company is hiring two developers.

vocab.definition: working for different clients, not employed by one company
vocab.example: He works freelance for foreign clients.

vocab.definition: a move to a higher position at work
vocab.example: She got a promotion last year.

quiz.prompt: The company wants to ___ three new engineers.
quiz.explanation: Hire = give someone a job. Fire = remove from a job.

quiz.prompt: Teamwork and communication are important ___.
I work ___ for several clients. (not employed)
My ___ helped me fix the bug.
"I am responsible of the team" is correct.

rememberErrors.why: Different preposition from French « responsable de ».

title: Articles (a, an, the, Ø) and prepositions of time and place
objective: Use articles correctly with general and specific nouns, and choose in / on / at.

sections.heading: a / an
sections.en: Use a/an with a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time, or with jobs. "An" before a vowel sound: an hour, an engineer, but a university (/juː/).
sections.fr: « an » se choisit selon le son, pas la lettre : an hour, a university.

sections.heading: the
sections.en: Use "the" when the listener knows which one: something mentioned before, unique things, or specified by the sentence.
examples: I bought a laptop. The laptop is very fast.
The sun is hot today.
The report you sent was excellent.

sections.heading: No article (Ø) for general meaning
sections.en: In English, general statements use NO article with plural and uncountable nouns. This is the most common error of French speakers.
sections.fr: Contrairement au français, on ne met PAS d'article pour une idée générale : « La vie est belle » → « Life is beautiful ».
examples: Life is short. (not: The life)
I love music.
Students need practice.
Technology changes quickly.

sections.heading: in / on / at
sections.en: Time and place.
table: at 6 o'clock, at night, at the weekend
at home, at work, at the station
on the table, on the second floor
in May, in 2027, in the morning
in Lomé, in the room, in Canada

vocab.example: Our office is on the third floor.

practice.explanation: General meaning of an uncountable noun → no article.

quiz.prompt: She is ___ engineer.
quiz.explanation: "Engineer" starts with a vowel sound → an.

quiz.prompt: I study at ___ university in Lomé.
quiz.explanation: "University" starts with the sound /juː/ (a consonant sound) → a.

quiz.prompt: My birthday is ___ June.
The meeting is on Friday ___ 10 a.m.
"The money is not everything" expresses a general idea correctly.
quiz.explanation: General meaning → no article: Money is not everything.

quiz.prompt: I'm ___ home now.
I watched a film yesterday. ___ film was boring.

rememberErrors.why: Choose a/an by sound, not by letter.

title: Comparatives and superlatives
objective: Compare people, places and things.

sections.heading: Short adjectives
sections.en: Add -er / -est: cheap → cheaper → the cheapest. Double the consonant: big → bigger. y → i: easy → easier.

sections.heading: Long adjectives
sections.en: more / the most + adjective: more expensive, the most beautiful. Use than after the comparative.
sections.fr: « plus … que » = -er than / more … than. Jamais « more cheaper ».
examples: Lomé is bigger than Kara.
This phone is more expensive than that one.
It's the best restaurant in town.

vocab.example: The market is more crowded on Saturday.
My village is quieter than the city.

practice.prompt: This is the ___ day of my life!

quiz.prompt: Flights are ___ than buses.
easy → ___ (comparative)
It's ___ hotel in the city.
"more better" is correct.
Today is ___ than yesterday. (bad)

title: Describing people
objective: Describe appearance and personality.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.en: tall / short · slim / overweight · long / short hair · curly / straight hair · He has got a beard. She wears glasses.
examples: My brother is tall and slim.
She's got long curly hair.

sections.heading: Personality
sections.en: friendly · shy · funny · kind · lazy · hard-working · generous. Ask: What's he like? (personality) / What does he look like? (appearance).
sections.fr: « What is he like? » = Comment est-il (caractère) ? Pas « Qu'est-ce qu'il aime ».

vocab.definition: working with a lot of effort
happy to give money or time

quiz.prompt: Someone who makes you laugh is…
quiz.explanation: Funny = someone who makes you laugh.

quiz.prompt: "What does he look like?" — "___"
She is nervous with new people. She is ___.
quiz.explanation: Shy = nervous with people you don't know.

quiz.prompt: "generous" describes someone who likes giving.
quiz.explanation: Generous people like giving money or time.

quiz.prompt: Hair that is not curly is…

rememberErrors.wrong: What is he like? (= his hobbies)

title: too, enough, too much, too many
objective: Say when something is a problem: too expensive, not big enough.

sections.heading: too / enough
sections.en: too + adjective (more than OK). adjective + enough (OK). not + adjective + enough (less than OK).
sections.fr: Attention à l'ordre : « big enough », pas « enough big ».
examples: This bag is too heavy.
The room isn't big enough.
Are you warm enough?

sections.heading: too much / too many / enough + noun
sections.en: too much + uncountable, too many + plural, enough + noun.
examples: There's too much noise.
There are too many cars.
We haven't got enough chairs.

practice.prompt: The coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it.

quiz.prompt: There are ___ people on the bus.
Which is correct?
We don't have ___ money for the tickets.
"too much traffic" is correct.
These shoes are ___ small. I need a bigger size.

title: At the doctor's
objective: Explain how you feel and understand simple advice.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.en: I've got a headache / a fever / a cough / a sore throat / stomach ache. I feel sick. My back hurts.
sections.fr: « J'ai mal à la tête » = I've got a headache. « J'ai mal au dos » = My back hurts.
examples: I've got a fever and a sore throat.
My leg hurts.

sections.heading: Advice
sections.en: You should rest. · Take this medicine twice a day. · Drink plenty of water. · Come back if it gets worse.
examples: You should stay in bed for two days.
Take one tablet after each meal.

vocab.definition: something you take to get better
a fixed time to see a doctor or someone

practice.explanation: A pain in your head is a headache.

quiz.prompt: My back ___.
A high body temperature is a ___.
quiz.explanation: A fever is a high body temperature.

quiz.prompt: A fixed time to see the doctor:
"I have mal at my head" is correct English.
"Take this twice a day" means…

rememberErrors.wrong: I have pain in my head.

title: Adverbs: how and how often
objective: Say how often and how people do things.

sections.heading: Frequency
sections.en: always · usually · often · sometimes · rarely · never. Before the main verb, after be.
sections.fr: Place : « I often go », mais « She is often late ».
examples: I usually get up at six.
He is never late.
We sometimes eat out.

sections.heading: Manner
sections.en: Adjective + -ly: quick → quickly, careful → carefully. Irregular: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard.
examples: She speaks English well.
Drive carefully!
He works hard.

options: I go often to the gym.
I often go to the gym.
practice.explanation: Frequency adverb before the main verb.

quiz.prompt: He is ___ on time. (100%)
quick → ___ (adverb)
Which is correct?
"He works hardly" means he works a lot.
quiz.explanation: hard = with effort; hardly = almost not.

quiz.prompt: Please drive ___.

rememberErrors.wrong: She speaks good English. / She speaks English good.

rememberErrors.why: Frequency adverb before the main verb.

title: Home and renting
objective: Describe your home and talk to a landlord.

sections.heading: Rooms and things
sections.en: living room · bedroom · kitchen · bathroom · balcony · fridge · fan · air conditioning · furniture.
examples: My flat has two bedrooms and a small balcony.
The fan in the bedroom doesn't work.

sections.heading: Renting
sections.en: rent (money per month) · landlord · tenant · deposit · bills (water, electricity) · furnished / unfurnished.
sections.fr: « loyer » = rent ; « propriétaire » = landlord.
examples: The rent is 80,000 francs a month.
Are bills included?

vocab.definition: a person who rents a home to you
vocab.example: I called the landlord about the leak.

vocab.definition: money you pay first and get back later
vocab.example: The deposit is two months' rent.

practice.prompt: Money you pay every month for a flat:
practice.explanation: Rent is the money you pay every month to live in a flat.
The kitchen is the room where you cook.

quiz.prompt: The person who owns the flat you rent:
quiz.explanation: The landlord owns the flat and rents it to you.

quiz.prompt: "furnitures" is correct.
Are the ___ (water, electricity) included?
quiz.explanation: Bills are what you pay for water, electricity, internet…

quiz.prompt: A flat with tables and beds is…
quiz.explanation: Furnished = it comes with furniture (tables, beds…).

quiz.prompt: Money you get back when you leave:
quiz.explanation: A deposit is paid at the start and returned when you leave.

title: and, but, because, so, when
objective: Connect ideas into longer sentences.

sections.heading: Linking words
sections.en: and (add) · but (contrast) · because (reason) · so (result) · when (time).
sections.fr: because + raison, so + conséquence. « donc » = so.
examples: I was tired, so I went to bed.
I went to bed because I was tired.
It's cheap but good.
When I arrived, they were eating.

vocab.example: I'm late because of the traffic.
It rained, so we stayed in.

quiz.prompt: The hotel was nice ___ expensive.
___ I was a child, I lived in Kara.
She didn't come ___ she was ill.
"I was tired, so I slept" shows a result.
It was late, ___ we took a taxi.

rememberErrors.right: I went home because I was tired.
rememberErrors.why: Because needs a main clause in writing.

rememberErrors.wrong: I was ill so I stay.
rememberErrors.right: I was ill, so I stayed.

title: Phone calls and messages
objective: Make a phone call and write a short message.

sections.heading: On the phone
sections.en: Hello, this is… · Can I speak to…? · Hold on, please. · She's not available. Can I take a message? · Could you call me back?
sections.fr: « C'est Ama » = This is Ama (pas « I am Ama »).
examples: Hello, this is Kofi. Can I speak to Mr Mensah?
Sorry, he's in a meeting. Can I take a message?

sections.heading: Short messages
sections.en: Hi / Dear… · Just to let you know… · Can you…? · Thanks! · See you soon / Best wishes.
examples: Hi Sena, just to let you know I'll be ten minutes late. Sorry! Kofi

vocab.definition: to phone someone who phoned you
vocab.example: Can you call me back later?

vocab.definition: to wait for a short time
information you send or leave for someone

practice.explanation: On the phone, say "This is…", not "I am…".
"Hold on" means wait a moment on the phone.

quiz.prompt: "Can I take a message?" means…
options: Can I write down your message for someone?

quiz.prompt: Could you call me ___ later? (phrasal verb)
quiz.explanation: call back = phone someone who phoned you.

quiz.prompt: "Can I speak to Ama?" is a polite phone question.
Informal ending for a message:
"Just to let you know…" introduces…

rememberErrors.wrong: Hello, I am Kofi. (on the phone)

title: Have you ever…? Experiences
objective: Talk about life experiences with the present perfect.

sections.heading: Form
sections.en: have / has + past participle. ever in questions, never in negatives.
sections.fr: Pas de date précise → present perfect. Avec une date → past simple.
examples: Have you ever been to Ghana? — Yes, I have.
I've never eaten snails.
She has visited Paris twice.

sections.heading: Common participles
sections.en: be → been · go → gone/been · eat → eaten · see → seen · do → done · try → tried · fly → flown.
examples: Have you ever flown in a plane?
I've tried fufu, and I loved it.

vocab.definition: at any time in your life

quiz.prompt: She ___ tried sushi.
Have you ever ___ (eat) attiéké?
I ___ to London in 2022.
"Have you ever see a lion?" is correct.
Two times =
quiz.explanation: Twice = two times (once, twice, three times).

rememberErrors.wrong: I have been in Accra last year.
rememberErrors.right: I went to Accra last year.

title: Booking a hotel
objective: Book a room, check in and ask for help.

sections.heading: Booking
sections.en: I'd like to book a single / double room for two nights. · Is breakfast included? · How much is it per night?
examples: I'd like to book a double room from Friday to Sunday.

sections.heading: At the hotel
sections.en: check in · check out · reception · key card · Wi-Fi password · room service.
sections.fr: check in = arriver et s'enregistrer ; check out = libérer la chambre.
examples: What time is check-out?
Could I have the Wi-Fi password, please?

quiz.prompt: I'd like to ___ a room for Saturday.
Is breakfast ___ in the price?
You check in when you arrive at the hotel.
Where do you get your key?
quiz.explanation: You get your key at reception, the front desk.

quiz.prompt: "How much is it per night?" asks about…

rememberErrors.wrong: I want to reserve me a room.
rememberErrors.right: I'd like to book a room.

title: must, have to, don't have to
objective: Talk about rules and obligations.

sections.heading: Obligation
sections.en: must / have to + verb = it's necessary. must = rule or personal feeling; have to = external rule.
examples: You must wear a seatbelt.
I have to work on Saturday.

sections.heading: Prohibition vs no obligation
sections.en: mustn't = it's not allowed. don't have to = it's not necessary.
sections.fr: Piège : « You don't have to come » = ce n'est pas obligatoire, PAS « tu ne dois pas venir ».
examples: You mustn't smoke here.
You don't have to pay — it's free.

vocab.example: Phones are not allowed in the exam.

vocab.definition: a belt that keeps you safe in a car

quiz.prompt: She ___ wear a uniform at work. (rule)
You ___ use your phone in the exam. (it's forbidden, contraction)
"You don't have to come" means you are not allowed to come.
___ I have to bring my passport?
I ___ to get up early tomorrow.

title: should: giving advice
objective: Give and ask for advice.

sections.heading: Form
sections.en: should / shouldn't + verb. Question: Should I…? Also: I think you should… / Why don't you…?
sections.fr: « Tu devrais » = you should.
examples: You should drink more water.
You shouldn't stay up late.
What should I do?
Why don't you ask your teacher?

vocab.definition: an opinion about what someone should do
vocab.example: Can you give me some advice?

practice.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed.

quiz.prompt: You ___ eat so much sugar.
What ___ I wear to the interview?
"an advice" is correct.
quiz.explanation: advice is uncountable: a piece of advice / some advice.

quiz.prompt: Why ___ you take a taxi?
She should ___ a doctor.

rememberErrors.right: some advice / a piece of advice

title: will: decisions, offers, promises
objective: Use will for quick decisions, offers and promises.

sections.heading: Uses of will
sections.en: Decision now: I'll have the chicken. Offer: I'll help you. Promise: I'll call you tonight. Prediction: It will be hot tomorrow.
sections.fr: going to = projet déjà décidé ; will = décision prise maintenant.
examples: The phone is ringing. — I'll answer it.
Don't worry, I won't tell anyone.
Will you marry me?

vocab.definition: to say you will certainly do something
vocab.example: I promise I'll be on time.

vocab.definition: to say you are willing to do something

practice.prompt: It's cold. — I ___ close the window.

quiz.prompt: That bag looks heavy. I ___ carry it for you.
I ___ call you when I arrive. (promise, full form)
"I will to help you" is correct.
quiz.explanation: will + base verb: I will help you.

quiz.prompt: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
Won't is the short form of…

rememberErrors.wrong: I call you later, I promise.
rememberErrors.right: I'll call you later, I promise.

title: Buying clothes
objective: Ask for sizes, try clothes on and return them.

sections.heading: In a clothes shop
sections.en: Can I try it on? · What size are you? · Do you have it in a bigger size / in blue? · It's too small. · It suits you.
examples: Can I try these trousers on?
Do you have this shirt in a medium?

sections.heading: Paying and returning
sections.en: the changing room · on sale · receipt · return · exchange.
sections.fr: « Ça te va bien » = It suits you.
examples: Keep the receipt if you want to return it.
Can I exchange this for a smaller size?

vocab.definition: to put on clothes to see if they fit
a paper that proves you paid

practice.prompt: You want to check if a shirt fits. You ask:
practice.explanation: try it on (pronoun in the middle).

practice.prompt: The paper that proves you paid:
practice.explanation: A receipt proves you paid (a recipe is for cooking).

quiz.prompt: Where do you try clothes on?
That dress really ___ you. (looks good on you)
"recipe" is the paper you get after paying.
quiz.explanation: That's a receipt; a recipe is for cooking.

quiz.prompt: Cheaper than usual:
quiz.explanation: On sale = at a lower price than usual.

quiz.prompt: Can I ___ this for a bigger size?

title: mine, yours, whose
objective: Talk about who owns things.

sections.heading: Possessive pronouns
sections.en: mine · yours · his · hers · ours · theirs. They replace adjective + noun.
examples: This bag is mine. (= my bag)
Is this phone yours?
Their house is bigger than ours.

sections.heading: Whose?
sections.en: Whose + noun asks about the owner. Answer with 's or a pronoun.
sections.fr: Ne pas confondre whose (à qui) et who's (who is).
examples: Whose keys are these? — They're Ama's.
Whose is this jacket? — It's mine.

vocab.example: This car belongs to my father.

quiz.prompt: Is this your book? — Yes, it's ___.
quiz.explanation: my book → mine (possessive pronoun, no noun after it).

quiz.prompt: Their car is red. ___ is blue.
This laptop belongs to Sena. It's ___. (pronoun)
"Who's bag is this?" is correct.
The house ___ to my uncle.

rememberErrors.right: This is my book. / This book is mine.

title: City life
objective: Describe your town and its good and bad points.

sections.heading: Places and features
sections.en: neighbourhood · traffic · pollution · public transport · nightlife · parks · crowded · noisy · safe.
examples: My neighbourhood is quiet and safe.
The traffic is terrible in the morning.

sections.heading: Good and bad points
sections.en: The best thing about… is… · One problem is… · There isn't enough…
examples: The best thing about Lomé is the beach.
One problem is the traffic.

vocab.definition: cars and vehicles on the road
dirt in the air or water

quiz.prompt: Buses and trains for everyone:
There's too much ___ — the roads are full of cars.
quiz.explanation: Traffic = cars and vehicles on the road (uncountable).

quiz.prompt: "nightlife" means bars, music and places to go in the evening.
quiz.explanation: Nightlife = places to go out in the evening.

quiz.prompt: The opposite of noisy:
quiz.explanation: Quiet is the opposite of noisy.

quiz.prompt: "The best thing ___ my town is the market."
